text:
incidents-bot: [PAGER] High GPU capacity pressure in azure-centralus - autoscaler failing to create new nodes, queue growth detected. Severity: P2. @Sara (oncall) paged.

Sara (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing sustained GPU util ~98% on pool: inference-centralus-gpu. Autoscaler logs show quotaExceeded errors from Azure for GPU SKU requests.

Mike: where's the traffic coming from? Hosted API or Dedicated?

Sara (oncall): Mostly hosted inference traffic; a few Dedicated customers had recent rollouts but traffic spike is global for centralus region. Queue length on request-queue metric up from ~30 -> ~860 in 12m. Errors are 429/503 for new requests.

Jia: can you paste the exact error from the autoscaler?

Sara (oncall): logs: 
```
2026-03-14T14:02:31Z autoscaler: failed to create 2 nodes: quotaExceeded: Quota 'GPUS' for region 'centralus' exceeded. Current limit: 64, requested: 72.
```
Also seeing Azure error id: 0xA3F1 in cloud logs.

Rohit: that matches the billing/limit view — we hit GPU quota 64. Recent Dedicated pool churn bumped usage. We didn't get proactive notif since usage spike happened fast.

Mike: impact table? Which customers affected and what's percent error rate on hosted API?

Sara (oncall): Hosted API 5.6% 503/429 across centralus; p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 480ms. Two Dedicated customers on reserved capacity saw increased tails and dropped requests but fallbacks to other regions are on for critical customers.

Jia: mitigation plan options: 1) failover some routing to westus or eastus2, 2) request quota increase from Azure support (slow), 3) temporarily scale down lower-priority batch jobs and free GPUs, 4) evict non-critical Dedicated VMs / preemptible instances.

Sara (oncall): I'm starting option 3+4 now: scaling down batch worker jobset and cordoning non-critical Dedicated nodes. Running: 
```
kubectl scale deployment batch-workers --replicas=2 -n infra-batch
kubectl cordon node dedicated-gpu-xx-??
```
Will post output.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: rollback of recent dedicated rollout (commit ab12f) to reduce peak usage.

Sara (oncall): rollback done, batch scaled. Freed ~8 GPUs according to cluster accounting. Queue growth slowed but still not fully under SLO. Autoscaler still failing for new node creation due to quota errors.

Rohit: Creating an emergency support ticket with Azure now. Using subscription id: 1234-REDACTED. Will request quota bump to 128 GPUs for centralus and ask for expedited review. Posting support link.

Rohit: done — support case #AZ-99281 created, priority: Critical, ETA 4-6 hours per portal. I also tried using alternate SKU (A100->V100) but model runtime pinned to A100 quantized builds; fallback would require model repack which is not feasible immediately.

Mike: while we wait, can we reroute a portion of hosted traffic to westus? How hard is that?

Jia: We have routing policy 'region-preference' in our router. I can flip a canary to send 20% of centralus traffic to westus. That should reduce pressure without impacting customers who pin region. Running: `infra-router patch policy region-preference --set canary=westus:20`

Sara (oncall): Can we prioritize critical customers for westus failover?

Jia: yes, policy supports customer-tier override. I'll apply: send all enterprise-tier requests to westus until further notice.

Jia: applied canary 20% + enterprise override. Monitoring dashboards paused-alarm?

Sara (oncall): Watching metrics — queue length down from 860 -> 420 over next 6m. Hosted error rate down to 2.1%. Enterprise customers showing normal behavior.

Mike: great. Any risk with cross-region latency for in-region customers? Need to inform support/ops.

Sara (oncall): minimal — westus median increase ~60ms for those routed. We have message template ready for status page. I'll draft a short update: "Partial degradation in centralus due to GPU quota limits; some traffic rerouted; limited errors persisted."

Rohit: Azure support responded: they acknowledged but can only increase to 80 within 2-3 hours via expedited channel. They asked for justification and workload details — provided.

Jia: can we free more capacity by terminating some non-critical Dedicated nodes? We already rolled back the recent rollout but some pinned nodes refuse eviction.

Sara (oncall): There's one customer pinning 12 GPUs for compliance reasons. I am coordinating with SE to request temporary relaxation — outbound email sent.

Rohit: update from support: they can raise quota to 96 within ~90 minutes if we provide an availability plan and confirm ability to distribute load across zones. I submitted that — waiting.

incidents-bot: note added to thread: incident created (#INC-2026-042), severity set P2, runbook link: /runbooks/gpu-quota-exhaustion.

Mike: we should also open a post-incident action item to add alerting on quota burn rate (not just capacity). Right now we trigger only on actual exhausted state.

Jia: agreed — add burn-rate alert and preemptive routing policy. Also propose automating eviction of lower-priority Dedicated nodes when quotaExceeded error appears.

Sara (oncall): Azure raised to 96 now per email at 14:58Z. Autoscaler retried and successfully created 2 nodes; cluster accounting shows current GPUs = 90/96. Queue down to 80, errors <0.5%.

Mike: handoff: I'm taking primary for follow-up. Sara — great job mitigating and coordinating. Please update incident doc with timelines and which customers had fallbacks. I'll synthesize RCA draft and coordinate postmortem.

Sara (oncall): handing off to Mike. I'll stay available for questions. Adding notes: actions taken, support case #AZ-99281, rollback commit, routing changes, customers contacted.

Rohit: filed follow-up action items: request baseline quota bump for centralus to 128, add burn-rate alert, automate low-priority eviction, add runbook steps for cross-region canary. Assigned to infra team.

Mike: closing loop on customer impact: Hosted API ~6% of requests in centralus saw elevated latency and transient 429/503 for ~35 minutes. Two Dedicated customers had degraded tails; both had fallbacks enabled and did not lose persistent data. Status page: updated.

incidents-bot: incident marked as "mitigated" at 15:05Z, will remain open for postmortem tracking.

Sara (oncall): tagging postmortem owners: Mike (lead), Jia (mitigations), Rohit (cloud quotas).

Mike: thanks team. I'll run the postmortem template tomorrow and schedule an IR follow-up.

Sara (oncall): thanks everyone :thumbsup:
